name: XL092
summary: XL092 is zanzalintinib, Exelixis's internally discovered oral multitargeted TKI (VEGFR, MET, TAM kinases), a different molecule from cabozantinib. The registrational trial is STELLAR-303 (NCT05425940, 901 patients): zanzalintinib 100 mg daily plus atezolizumab against regorafenib in previously treated non-MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer, which met overall survival in the ITT population (HR 0.80, median 10.9 vs 9.4 months; Lancet 2025). The NDA was accepted in February 2026 and its PDUFA date moved from 3 December 2026 to 3 March 2027. Price anchor: Stivarga, the control arm and the incumbent oral VEGFR TKI in this line, at $55,963 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: regorafenib's measured 14.8% of US post-chemotherapy treatment starts in pMMR/non-MSI-H mCRC (Desai et al., Future Oncol 2025). Only colorectal cancer is modelled: the nccRCC Phase 3 (STELLAR-304, NCT05678673) has not read out (primary completion 2026-12), the context lists its indication at Phase 1, and the book carries no renal cell pool.

therapy_mode.source: Hecht JR et al., 'Zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab versus regorafenib in refractory colorectal cancer (STELLAR-303): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial', Lancet 2025;406(10517):2360-2370, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(25)02025-2, PMID 41130252: oral zanzalintinib 100 mg daily plus IV atezolizumab 1200 mg every 3 weeks
therapy_mode.note: Oncology treated to progression, so chronic by the house definition

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Stivarga: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $96,423,433.02 over 1,723 beneficiaries = $55,963 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator, house convention. Stivarga (regorafenib) is the STELLAR-303 control arm, the oral VEGFR multikinase inhibitor zanzalintinib replaces in third-line mCRC, and the only drug in this line in the book's demand table (Fruzaqla and Lonsurf are not carried). The engine bills each start as at least one patient-year, so a per-beneficiary spend is the right kind of figure for a short course. The case against: a Stivarga beneficiary's spend reflects regorafenib's short time on drug (median PFS 2.0 months in the STELLAR-303 control arm), while zanzalintinib's is 3.7 months, so this understates spend per zanzalintinib patient. Stivarga's beneficiaries also include GIST and HCC use. Cabometyx, Exelixis's own oral TKI, reads $132,512 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Cabometyx), but that is mostly long-duration first-line RCC, not this setting. Atezolizumab is billed by Roche under Part B and is not Exelixis revenue

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS negotiated net prices)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is $27,981 per patient-year. Zanzalintinib is oral, so Part D is the right part. Case against: oncology is a Part D protected class and its brands usually rebate less than the median Part D brand, so 0.5 may overstate the discount

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: STELLAR-303 ITT: median PFS 3.7 months on zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab against 2.0 months on regorafenib (Exelixis release on the ESMO 2025 presentation, ir.exelixis.com/news-releases/news-release-details/exelixis-announces-detailed-results-phase-3-stellar-303-pivotal; Targeted Oncology, targetedonc.com/view/stellar-303-zanza-atezo-improves-os-in-pretreated-msi-stable-mcrc; full report Hecht JR et al., 'Zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab versus regorafenib in refractory colorectal cancer (STELLAR-303): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial', Lancet 2025;406(10517):2360-2370, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(25)02025-2, PMID 41130252)
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/3.7) = 0.894, the form the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed uses on its 5.3-month median in the same pool. The brief's 1 - exp(-12/3.7) gives 0.961; it treats the median as a mean, so it was not used. Case against: median duration of treatment was not found and can differ from PFS; grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 60% of patients (Lancet abstract) point to earlier stops, while treatment beyond progression on an immunotherapy combination points to later ones. The PFS figures were read from the release and trade press, not from the paper's full text

forecast_start_year.source: Exelixis 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0000939767-26-000098): NDA submitted December 2025, accepted February 2026 with a standard review and a PDUFA date of 3 December 2026; extended by three months to 3 March 2027 after a major amendment (cancernetwork.com/view/fda-extends-review-of-zanzalintinib-combo-in-pretreated-metastatic-crc). NCT05425940 primary completion 2026-06-16 (actual, book trials table)
forecast_start_year.note: The brief's default: the first year after the current one, and approval is due inside it. Judgement: approval on 3 March 2027 leaves about ten months of 2027 on market. Case against: 2028 is the first full year, and a complete response letter would push the start later. Exelixis reports pre-launch marketing spend in the same 10-Q

exus_multiple.source: Exelixis 10-K FY2025 (0000939767-26-000021): Exelixis retains all global commercial rights to zanzalintinib; cabozantinib is sold outside the US by Ipsen and Takeda and reaches Exelixis as royalties. The book's asset_revenue_regions holds no split for any Exelixis product
exus_multiple.note: Null: no sourceable ex-US revenue for Exelixis. It has no commercial organisation outside the US, no ex-US filing for zanzalintinib appears in the Q2 2026 10-Q, and no partner is named. A multiple built on Ipsen's Cabometyx sales would describe a partner's revenue, and any future ex-US deal would likely pay Exelixis a royalty rather than product revenue. The engine then models the US alone, which understates value if Exelixis later licenses ex-US rights

economics_share.source: Exelixis 10-K FY2025 (0000939767-26-000021): zanzalintinib is 'the furthest along of our internally-discovered small molecule product candidates' and 'we continue to retain all global commercial and marketing rights to zanzalintinib' (repeated in the Q2 2026 10-Q, 0000939767-26-000098, and the Exelixis-Merck clinical collaboration release, October 2024, ir.exelixis.com/news-releases/news-release-details/exelixis-and-merck-sign-clinical-development-collaboration)
economics_share.note: No licensor and no royalty payable found. The GSK royalty now held by Royalty Pharma attaches to 'any product containing cabozantinib' only (same 10-K). Roche supplies atezolizumab under a clinical collaboration and books its own atezolizumab sales; nothing in the filings gives Roche a share of zanzalintinib

prevalence.source: carried by the book: 158,850 (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, 2026 new US cases), telisotuzumab adizutecan and PF-08634404 seeds
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. The pool is the year's own diagnoses (prevalence equals incidence)

incidence.source: carried by the book: 158,850 (SEER), as above

eligible_pct.source: Three filters, the first two reused from the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed by name. (1) 35.1% metastatic, that seed's SEER derivation. (2) 4,407 of 22,078 US mCRC patients (19.96%) received a third line after two lines of standard chemotherapy (Nevala-Plagemann et al., J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2023, doi:10.6004/jnccn.2022.7082). (3) STELLAR-303 excluded MSI-H/dMMR tumours: 153 dMMR among 3,063 first-line mCRC trial patients, 5.0% (Venderbosch et al., Clin Cancer Res 2014, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0332, the PF-08634404 seed's source), leaving 95.0%. 0.351 x 0.1996 x 0.9500 = 0.0666, about 10,570 patients a year
eligible_pct.note: The sought label is metastatic CRC previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin- and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, and an anti-EGFR if RAS wild-type (CancerNetwork on the NDA acceptance), the same third-line population as the regorafenib, trifluridine/tipiracil and fruquintinib labels. Cross-check: Takeda puts US third-line and later mCRC at 14,600 patients (HUTCHMED filing, as returned by search, not opened), which counts fourth-line patients again. Case for a larger pool: dMMR is rarer by third line than in first-line trials, because most dMMR patients now get immunotherapy first and many respond durably. Case for a smaller one: 28.8% of post-chemotherapy pMMR patients get best supportive care only (Desai et al., below), and Nevala-Plagemann counts only those treated

untreated_carryover_pct.source: forecast.py convention for a line of cancer therapy (patients_for_indication)
untreated_carryover_pct.note: A third-line patient not started on zanzalintinib starts another regimen and leaves the line. Stated for clarity: the book's pool has prevalence equal to incidence, so the engine would set 0 and no opening pool anyway

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: Regorafenib took 30 of 203 (14.8%) pMMR/non-MSI-H mCRC patients who started systemic therapy after all three standard chemotherapies, and trifluridine/tipiracil 25 of 203 (12.3%), US Oncology Network iKnowMed records 2016-2021 with chart review (Desai et al., 'Biomarker testing, treatment patterns and outcomes in previously treated pMMR or non-MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer patients', Future Oncol 2025;21(16):2027-2037, doi:10.1080/14796694.2025.2504246, PMID 40371599, full text PMC12218554)
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: 1.0x regorafenib's measured capture, the incumbent zanzalintinib beat head to head on overall survival (HR 0.80). The denominator is treated patients, the same basis as Nevala-Plagemann's third-line count in eligible_pct. Case for higher: the first immunotherapy-based regimen with an OS gain in non-MSI-H mCRC, sold by a company already calling on these oncologists with Cabometyx; a new entrant in this line can grow fast (Fruzaqla in-market sales $290.6mm in 2024 and $366.2mm in 2025, HUTCHMED 20-F FY2025 0001104659-26-023822, as returned by search, not opened); and a drug used in fourth line also reaches patients counted once here. Case for lower: the 2016-2021 data predate trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab and fruquintinib (both 2023), so the line now splits more ways; grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 60% vs 37% on regorafenib; the co-primary endpoint in patients without liver metastases missed at the final analysis (HR 0.83, p=0.1185, Q2 2026 10-Q); and IV atezolizumab every 3 weeks adds infusion visits to an otherwise oral line

ramp_steepness.source: book: Enhertu's CMS Part B launch fit (864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 beneficiaries 2020-2024), k=1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, as carried by the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed in this pool
ramp_steepness.note: Reused measured oncology curve from the closest modelled competitor in the same pool. No colorectal launch curve is in the book (Fruzaqla is not in the demand table). Case against: Exelixis already sells to these oncologists, and an OS-positive late-line drug can ramp faster than a multi-indication ADC

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Enhertu fit carried by the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed)
